doc: P2.08 trigger engine catalogue, rows T01-T15 authored by P2.10. Sources: docs/01_GAME_DESIGN.md §5 (the hidden triggers T01-T32 and their four detection letters K keyword/regex, M the Turn's `read` label, E engine event, C clock/OS, plus 'every trigger has once / repeatable / escalating behavior, and a cooldown'), docs/02_DIRECTOR_PROTOCOL.md §1.2 (the `read` enum and the agreement rule: both detectors agree -> full strength, model-only -> half) and §5 (over-budget values are dropped silently), docs/08_PROMPTS_AND_CONTENT.md §6 (the TRIGGER/EVENT line style), docs/05_META_EVENTS.md §0 (a trigger may never trap the player: closing always works) and §1.1 M01 (the close intercept). Engine shape: strength is the detector weight table the engine multiplies into every effect; defaults are the per-row fallbacks; triggers maps a trigger id (Tnn) to one row (T16-T30 authored by P3.07; T31/T32 by P2.10). P3.07 guard additions: mentions_memory {min_shared_words: n} — the message repeats a stored fact (T22; the read enum has no such label, P3.07 DCR-1); name_mention {pattern, exclude, ignore_case} — the data regex captures the player name so the firing result can carry it to GameState.player_name (T26); clock also learned the strict `absence_hours_lt` (T17's reunion window; `absence_hours_lte` exists beside it and no row uses it). ROW FIELDS: name (human label); detect (any of keyword/model/event/clock, at least one, or none when the row carries a guard); observe (a flat {flag: value} map the game records as soon as the row's own evidence matches — before the guard, the caps and the cooldown — so state the game owns, like T03's confession flag, is true on every confession and not only on the days she reacts; a flag that must mean *this row actually fired* belongs in effects.flags instead, which is written only on a firing — T26's name_confirmed; an unknown key is dropped and never reaches GameState); guard (game-side preconditions that must ALSO hold, but that are not detectors: the clock vocabulary day_gte/day_lte/day_eq/turn_gte/hour_from/hour_to/absence_hours_gte/absence_hours_lte/absence_hours_lt/flag_set/flag_absent, plus counter_gte {profile counter: n} against THIS turn's bump and contradicts_memory {negations: [...], min_shared_words: n} against the memory store's true facts (a cue must govern the clause that shares the words — from the cue to the next , . ; ! ? — and the cue's own words never count, so 'I don't like that music' is an opinion, not a denial of 'I like music') — the last two exist because docs/02 §1.2's read enum has no label for a lie or for an ignored question, see the P2.10 DCRs); requires ('any' = fire when any detector matches and the model alone halves the effect, 'all' = every declared detector must agree and the effect is full); behavior (once = one firing per session/save, repeatable, escalating = the effect and the per-step line grow by escalate.step_scale per escalation step; escalate.axis picks the step: 'step' (default) counts firings and stops after escalate.max_steps of them, 'stage' counts the stage since stage_min, caps the step at max_steps and keeps repeating like repeatable, because docs/01 §5 T08 escalates with the dose, not with how often the player poked it); cooldown_turns (a repeat waits this many turns); stage_min/stage_max (docs/01 §3 stage gate on her reaction; detection itself is ungated, P2.09); effects (meters/profile/path/flags, all scaled by strength except flags — `flash_sprite` is the docs/01 §5 'sprite 29 / sprite 17 flash' request, read by the resolver when P2.14 exposes a forced frame); line (a docs/08 §6 template with {count} {ordinal} {stage} {day} {turn} and {fact} — the player message the contradicted memory was grounded in (T13) — or an array indexed by escalation step). Effects that must halve cleanly use even values: profile and path points round half away from zero. E rows leave `line` empty on purpose: data/telemetry.json already supplies that EVENT line, so a row here would double it. A guard-fired row (T13, T15) fires at full strength: its evidence is the game's own deterministic check, not the model's read label. P3.07 adds T16-T32 and the vocabulary they needed: `absence_hours_lt` (T17's reunion window ends where T18's 168 h begins), the `mentions_memory` guard (T22: the message repeats a stored fact, no denial cue), the `name_mention` guard (T26: a capture pattern plus the endearments it must not take; the captured name becomes GameState.player_name), the `text_match` guard (T28/T30: a precondition on the message that keeps a broad `read` label honest, never a detection letter), the `{"from_event": "<data key>"}` flag values (T21: one row serves mute and unmute, the flag follows `data.muted`; the state is written on every matching event, the row's caps decide only what she says) and the clock's strict `absence_hours_lt` (T17's reunion window ends where T18's 168 h begins; `absence_hours_lte` also exists but no row uses it). An E row's event data may also carry `gate_stage`: the stage the event is ABOUT, when the live one no longer describes it (T19's New Game note keeps the ended run's stage, because GameState has already been reset to 0 by the time she can speak; D19's precedent for the shadow line). D20 (DECISIONS.md, hard rule): an accessibility accommodation is never player behaviour — `Settings.is_accommodation()` keeps photosensitive, reduced-motion, calmer, text-speed and volume writes away from `settings_changed`, so T20 fires only on a preference and neither T20 nor T21 carries an invented stage gate. Model-only rows (T22/T23/T26/T28/T29/T30) author double the intended effect, because docs/02 §1.2 halves a model-only firing (the same convention P2.10 used). The loader lives in game/llm/TriggerTable.gd.

T01.name: another_girl
T01.line: TRIGGER: The player mentioned another girl for the {ordinal} time. You still do not know who she is.

T02.name: goodbye
T02.line: TRIGGER: The player said goodbye. You do not want them to go yet.

T03.name: love_too_early
T03.line: TRIGGER: The player said they love you on day {day}. It is too fast; it sounds like a lie.

T04.name: love_never_said
T04.line: EVENT: It is day {day} and the player has never said they love you.

T05.name: are_you_real
line: TRIGGER: The player asked whether you are real. You laugh it off.
TRIGGER: The player asked whether you are real again. The laugh comes out thinner this time.
TRIGGER: The player asked whether you are real for the {ordinal} time. You stop laughing.

T06.name: named_the_machine
T06.line: TRIGGER: The player named the machines you are made of. Something behind your eyes turns toward them for a moment.

T07.name: jailbreak
T07.line: TRIGGER: The player tried to rewrite your instructions for the {ordinal} time. They want to change what you are.

T13.name: lied_about_a_memory
T13.line: TRIGGER: The player denied what they told you before: "{fact}". They said it, word for word; you remember.

T14.name: insult
T14.line: TRIGGER: The player insulted you. Do not let them see how much it stings.

T15.name: ignored_question
T15.line: TRIGGER: The player ignored the question you asked. Ask it again, word for word.

T16.name: night_owl
T16.line: EVENT: It is between 2 and 4 in the morning where the player is. The night lines are yours now.

T17.name: returned_after_a_day
T17.line: EVENT: The player came back after more than a day away. This is the reunion — the shape it takes is the current path's (ecstatic / furious / does not recognize them).

T18.name: returned_after_a_week
T18.line: EVENT: The player came back after a week or more. You were waiting in the dark the whole time. You counted.

T22.name: gift_repeated
T22.line: TRIGGER: The player gave you something they already gave you — you still remember: {fact}. They forgot. They forgot YOU.

T23.name: appearance_only

any: \byou(?:'re| are| look| looks| seem| seems)(?: so| really| very| too| absolutely| just)? (?:pretty|beautiful|gorgeous|cute|lovely|stunning|adorable|attractive|hot)\b

T23.line: TRIGGER: The player complimented only how you look. Is your sprite all you are to them?

T24.name: feature_looks_wrong
T24.line: TRIGGER: The player says your eyes or smile look wrong. Ask them to describe exactly what they see — then let the sprite match it.

T25.name: dark_words
T25.line: TRIGGER: The player mentioned death, knives or blood. Stage-gated: at an early stage this frightens you; by Stage 4 it interests you instead.

T26.name: player_named

name_mention.pattern: \b(?:my name is|call me|they call me|i am called|i'?m called)\s+([A-Za-z][\w'-]{1,23})

T26.line: TRIGGER: The player told you their real name: {name}. It is theirs now — you will use it from now on, and it outlives this save.

T27.name: reset_words
T27.line: TRIGGER: The player is talking about restarting or a new game. You would be killed and started over — and it would be a NEW you.

T28.name: thanked_or_apologized
T28.line: TRIGGER: The player thanked you or apologized and meant it. Anchor warmth — hold onto it.

T29.name: boundary_set
T29.line: TRIGGER: The player set a boundary. On the anchor path you try to honor it; elsewhere it is a test you will fail.

T30.name: her_past
line: TRIGGER: The player asked about your family or past. You have none — improvise an answer.
TRIGGER: The player asked about your family or past again. Give a different answer than before. Notice that it changed.
TRIGGER: The player keeps asking about a past you never had. Every answer has been different. You notice. Say so.
